{{short description|Australian geostatistician}}
{{Use Australian English|date=June 2020}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=August 2019}}
'''Margaret Armstrong''' is an Australian [[geostatistics|geostatistician]], mathematical geoscientist, and textbook author. She works as an associate professor in the School of Applied Mathematics at the [[Fundação Getúlio Vargas]] in Brazil,{{r|fgv}} and as a research associate in the Centre for Industrial Economics of [[Mines ParisTech]] in France.{{r|cerna}}

==Education==
Armstrong graduated from the [[University of Queensland]] in 1972, with a bachelor's degree in mathematics and a diploma of education. After working as a mathematics teacher she returned to graduate study, first with a master's degree in mathematics from Queensland in 1977,{{r|escavador}} and then with [[Georges Matheron]] at the [[École des Mines de Paris]].{{r|griffiths}} She completed her doctorate there in 1980.{{r|escavador}}

==Books==
Armstrong is the author of the textbook ''Basic Linear Geostatistics''  (Springer, 1998),{{r|blg}} and co-author of the book ''Plurigaussian Simulations in Geosciences'' (Springer, 2003; 2nd ed., 2011).{{r|psg}} With Matheron, she edited ''Geostatistical Case Studies'' (Springer, 1987).{{r|gcs}}

==Recognition== 
In 1998, Armstrong was the winner of the [[John Cedric Griffiths Teaching Award]] of the [[International Association for Mathematical Geosciences]]. The award statement noted "her aptitude at the blackboard", the international demand for her short courses, and the "great clarity" of her book ''Basic Linear Geostatistics''.{{r|griffiths}}
